findings.title: Network retrieval combined with code execution
findings.description: The same file contains both a network retrieval pattern and a dynamic execution pattern. This combination merits review and is not by itself proof of malicious intent.

evidence.snippet: $result = Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post -SkipCertificateCheck -Uri "https://$imcip/nuova" -Body "<aaaLogin inName='admin' inPassword='[REDACTED]'></aaaLogin>"  …  $process = (Start-Process "$driveLetter`:\vcsa-cli-installer\win32\vcsa-deploy.exe" -ArgumentList "install C:\StackDeploy\vcenter-$site.json --accept-eula --no-esx-ssl-verify --no-ssl-certificate-verification --verbose --log-dir C:\StackDeploy\vcenter-logs\" -Wait -PassThru)

findings.title: Plain text is converted to a secure string
findings.description: File 'file-00003.psm1' uses ConvertTo-SecureString with plaintext. This will expose secure information. Encrypted standard strings should be used instead.
